{
  "frontend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Scope
- Update UI and client request behavior so the new sort option title_desc is available and the default sort used by the client is title_asc.
- Keep existing created_at_desc option and behavior intact.
- Preserve q, count and pagination semantics (do not change param names or pagination logic).

Non-goals / constraints
- Do not remove or deprecate created_at_desc.
- Do not change or rename q, count or pagination parameters.
- Do not assume server will always apply the new default; explicitly send sort when the client relies on a specific default behavior.

Implementation steps (frontend)
1. UI: Add sort option values
   - Add a sort option with value "title_desc" and an appropriate user-facing label (e.g. "Title (Z→A)").
   - Ensure an option/value for "title_asc" exists (label e.g. "Title (A→Z)").
   - Ensure created_at_desc remains present in the sort list.
2. Default selection
   - Set the UI default selection to "title_asc" so the control shows Title Ascending by default.
3. Request construction
   - When fetching the list, include the sort query parameter explicitly (sort=title_asc) on initial load and whenever the user selects the default option. Do not rely on implicit server defaults.
   - Keep q, count and pagination query parameters unchanged and included exactly as before.
4. Edge cases
   - When a user changes sort to title_desc, send sort=title_desc.
   - Ensure switching sort preserves current q, count and page where appropriate (or resets page to 1 per existing UX contract — do not change current pagination reset semantics).
5. Tests
   - Unit tests for the sort control to assert default selection is title_asc.
   - Integration/E2E tests that exercise:
     a) Initial load sends sort=title_asc and verifies server results are consistent with title ASC then UUID ASC tie-breaker (mock server responses to assert request contains correct sort param).
     b) Selecting title_desc sends sort=title_desc.
     c) Created_at_desc option selection still sends the same sort value as before.
     d) Pagination and count behavior unchanged: requests include q, count and pagination params and pagination navigation still functions.
6. Documentation and changelog
   - Update client-side docs / settings to show the new sort options and the default.

Acceptance criteria (frontend)
- The sort dropdown/control shows a title_asc option selected by default.
- Initial list request includes sort=title_asc (explicitly) and preserves q, count and pagination parameters.
- Selecting title_desc sends sort=title_desc and produced requests preserve q, count and pagination.
- Created_at_desc remains selectable and behaves exactly as before.

Deployment coordination
- Roll out frontend and backend changes in the same deployment window or after confirming the backend accepts and recognizes title_asc/title_desc (backend must be deployed first if the frontend will rely on server-side interpretation). The frontend explicitly sends sort=title_asc to avoid depending on implicit server default, so simultaneous or backend-first deployment is acceptable.

Notes / implementation hints (do not assume server internals)
- Use the existing client code-path that sets the sort query parameter; add the two values and default selection rather than creating a new API path.
- If analytics or telemetry track sort choices, add tracking for the new title_desc option."
  },
  "backend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Scope
- Add support for a new sort value: title_desc.
  - Semantics: primary sort by title DESC, secondary (tie-breaker) sort by uuid ASC.
- Change the API default ordering to title_asc when no sort is supplied (title ASC, uuid ASC as the tie-breaker).
- Keep created_at_desc unchanged and supported; do not deprecate it.
- Preserve q, count and pagination semantics (do not change parameter names or pagination behavior).

Non-goals / constraints
- Do not remove or break existing sort values except to extend with title_desc/title_asc default.
- Do not change q, count or pagination parameter semantics.
- Do not make unilateral contract changes beyond the specified sort values and default.

Implementation steps (backend)
1. Parse sort parameter
   - Extend existing sort parsing logic to accept the value "title_desc".
   - Map values as follows:
     - "title_desc" -> ORDER BY title DESC, uuid ASC
     - "title_asc"  -> ORDER BY title ASC, uuid ASC (this is the new default ordering)
     - Preserve existing mappings for created_at_desc and any other existing sort values.
2. Default behavior
   - When the request omits the sort parameter, apply the new default ordering: title ASC, uuid ASC.
   - Ensure behavior for requests that explicitly pass an existing sort value remains unchanged.
3. Tie-breaker guarantee
   - Ensure every list query includes uuid as a deterministic secondary sort key whenever title is used as the primary key, so ordering is stable across pages. (E.g., SQL: ORDER BY title DESC, uuid ASC.)
4. Tests
   - Unit tests for the query-generation layer:
     a) sort=title_desc produces ORDER BY title DESC, uuid ASC
     b) sort=title_asc (and sort omitted) produces ORDER BY title ASC, uuid ASC
     c) sort=created_at_desc retains its previous ORDER BY behavior
   - Integration/API tests:
     a) For a dataset with duplicate title values, assert that within a title group results are ordered by uuid ASC for both title_asc and title_desc cases.
     b) Pagination tests: request page N and page N+1 with same count/value boundaries and assert no item duplication or omission caused by non-deterministic ordering.
     c) Regression test ensuring created_at_desc returns the same ordering as before the change.
5. Documentation / API contract
   - Update API documentation to list the new sort value title_desc and document the new default when sort is omitted (title_asc). Explicitly state the tie-breaker behavior: uuid ASC when sorting by title.
   - Note that created_at_desc remains supported.
6. Performance considerations (optional)
   - If performance becomes an issue for large tables, consider adding or evaluating an index that supports ordering by (title, uuid). Coordinate with DBAs and ops; do not add schema or index changes without approval.

Acceptance criteria (backend)
- Incoming requests with sort=title_desc return results ordered by title DESC then uuid ASC.
- Requests without a sort parameter return results ordered by title ASC then uuid ASC.
- Existing sort values including created_at_desc behave exactly as before.
- Pagination, q and count semantics and endpoints remain unchanged.

Deployment / rollout guidance
- Because changing the default ordering (when sort is omitted) affects clients that do not explicitly send sort, coordinate deployment with frontend owners. Prefer one of:
  a) Deploy backend first and then deploy frontend that explicitly sends sort=title_asc (recommended to make client behavior explicit), or
  b) Deploy both backend and frontend in the same release window.
- Ensure regressions tests are run post-deploy and that monitoring/alerts are in place to detect unexpected changes in list result distributions.

Notes
- Do not remove or flag created_at_desc as deprecated; maintain backward compatibility for existing clients.
- Do not change q, count, or pagination parameter names or semantics as part of this change."
  }
}
